claim: Regular sessions begin the second Wednesday of January each year
quote: Regular sessions of the Legislature shall commence on the second Wednesday of January of each year.

claim: In 1973 and every fourth year after, the Legislature organizes in January and recesses to the second Wednesday of February
quote: When all of these matters have been completed in the year one thousand nine hundred seventy-three and every fourth year thereafter, the Legislature shall adjourn until the second Wednesday of February following.

claim: Sessions are limited to sixty calendar days unless extended by two-thirds
quote: the regular session held in all other years shall not exceed sixty calendar days computed from and including the second Wednesday of January

claim: The governor must convene the Legislature on written application of three fifths of each house
quote: It shall be his duty to convene it, on application in writing, of three fifths of the members elected to each house.

claim: A bill not returned within five days (Sundays excepted) becomes law
quote: Any bill which shall not be returned by the governor within five days, Sundays excepted, after it shall have been presented to him shall be a law

claim: After adjournment sine die the governor has fifteen days (Sundays excepted) to file objections
quote: within fifteen days, Sundays excepted, after such adjournment, or become a law

claim: Acts take effect ninety days after passage unless two-thirds of each house direct otherwise
quote: shall take effect until the expiration of ninety days after its passage

claim: General elections are on the Tuesday after the first Monday in November of each even year
quote: General elections shall be held in the several election precincts of the state on the Tuesday next after the first Monday in November of each even year.

claim: All municipal elections must be held with a statewide primary or general election
quote: all local municipal elections shall be held concurrently with a regularly scheduled statewide primary or general election

claim: Municipalities negotiate an agreement with the county commission to move their elections
quote: a municipality shall negotiate an agreement with the county commission to establish the election date

claim: Regular municipal elections follow the § 3-1-31 timing
quote: the regular election of officers shall be held on the same day and in the same manner as prescribed by §3-1-31 of this code

claim: Charters with conflicting election days must conform by 1 July 2032
quote: shall amend said charter or otherwise revise its governing election provisions to make the requirements set forth in §3-1-31 of this code effective by July 1, 2032

claim: Municipalities may stagger or change officer terms by ordinance
quote: Municipalities may stagger and/or change the terms of elected municipal officers.

claim: Primary elections are on the second Tuesday in May of even years
quote: on the second Tuesday in May 1986 and in each second year thereafter

claim: County board of education members are elected at the primary, on a nonpartisan ballot
quote: An election for the purpose of electing members of the county board of education shall be held on the same date as the primary elections, as provided by law, but upon a nonpartisan ballot printed for the purpose.

claim: No more than two school board members may come from the same magisterial district
quote: No more than two members may be elected or serve from the same magisterial district.

claim: School board full terms are four years
quote: declared elected for full terms of four years

claim: Each county board of education has five members elected without party
quote: which shall be composed of five members, nominated and elected by the voters of the respective county without reference to political party affiliation

claim: Magistrates and circuit judges are elected at the primary on a nonpartisan ballot
quote: an election for the purpose of electing magistrates, shall be upon a nonpartisan ballot printed for the purpose

claim: Magistrates are elected by division at the primary on a nonpartisan ballot
quote: An election for the purpose of electing a magistrate or magistrates by division shall be held on the same date as the primary election

claim: Sheriff, prosecuting attorney, surveyor and assessor are elected every four years at the general election
quote: a sheriff, prosecuting attorney, surveyor of lands, and the number of assessors prescribed by law for the county

claim: A county commissioner is elected at every even-year general election
quote: every second year thereafter, a commissioner of the county commission for each county

claim: County clerk and circuit clerk are elected every six years
quote: every sixth year thereafter, a clerk of the county commission and a clerk of the circuit court for each county

claim: Party candidates for county offices are nominated at the primary
quote: and of each county in the state shall be nominated by the voters of the different political parties

claim: A plurality is enough for nomination in a primary
quote: In primary elections a plurality of the votes cast shall be sufficient for the nomination of candidates for office.

claim: A primary voter receives their party's ballot plus nonpartisan ballots
quote: In primary elections the ballot of the voter's political party at that election in that precinct shall be furnished to the voter together with separate ballots, if any, on any nonpartisan candidates

claim: Under the statute, a voter registered independent receives only nonpartisan ballots and questions in a primary
quote: he shall not, in a primary election, be given or entitled to vote any party ballot

claim: A losing primary candidate may not become another party's candidate for the same office
quote: may not, after failing to win the nomination of that political party at a primary election, become a candidate of any other recognized political party for the same political office

claim: A municipality may let municipal parties that are not state parties take part in its primary
quote: may participate in the primary elections of any such municipality

claim: Groups with no party organization nominate by certificate, for candidates not already in the primary
quote: Groups of citizens having no party organization may nominate candidates who are not already candidates in the primary election

claim: Certificate signers must be registered voters residing in the political division of the office
quote: who must be residents within the county, district, or other political division represented by the office sought

claim: The certificate filing rules do not apply to nonpartisan elections
quote: This section is inapplicable to nonpartisan elections.

claim: Each county has a county commission of three commissioners, unless reformed
quote: there shall be in each county of the state a county commission, composed of three commissioners

claim: Commissioners are elected countywide for six-year staggered terms, one every two years, no two from the same magisterial district
quote: so that one shall be elected every two years; but no two of said commissioners shall be elected from the same magisterial district

claim: Commissioners are elected by the voters of the county for six years
quote: The commissioners shall be elected by the voters of the county, and hold their office for a term of six years

claim: Counties elect a surveyor, prosecuting attorney, sheriff and one or two assessors for four years
quote: The voters of each county shall elect a surveyor of lands, a prosecuting attorney, a sheriff, and one and not more than two assessors, who shall hold their respective offices for the term of four years.

claim: A sheriff may not serve more than two consecutive terms
quote: shall be ineligible for the office of sheriff during any part of the term immediately following the second of the two consecutive terms

claim: Each county elects a clerk of the county commission for six years
quote: The voters of each county shall elect a clerk of the county commission, whose term of office shall be six years.

claim: The Legislature may reform a county commission on a county's application and voter approval
quote: with the assent of a majority of the voters of such county voting at an election, create another tribunal

claim: A county council created since 2008 as an alternative has four or more members
quote: shall consist of four or more members, a majority of whom shall constitute a quorum for the transaction of business

claim: A county commission has three commissioners
quote: A county commission shall consist of three commissioners

claim: A commission candidate must live in the magisterial district they seek by the filing deadline
quote: A candidate for the office of county commissioner shall be a resident from the magisterial district for which he or she is seeking election

claim: Municipalities are in four classes by population
quote: all municipal corporations are hereby classified by population into four classes

claim: Class I is over 50,000
quote: Every municipal corporation with a population in excess of fifty thousand shall be a Class I city

claim: Class II is over 10,000 to 50,000
quote: Every municipal corporation with a population in excess of ten thousand but not in excess of fifty thousand shall be a Class II city

claim: Class III is over 2,000 to 10,000
quote: Every municipal corporation with a population in excess of two thousand but not in excess of ten thousand shall be a Class III city

claim: Class IV, 2,000 or fewer, is a town or village
quote: Every municipal corporation with a population of two thousand or less shall be a Class IV town or village.

claim: Class changes automatically with the census
quote: Transition from one to another class shall occur automatically when the requisite population qualification has been met

claim: Municipalities over 2,000 may frame and adopt their own charters
quote: the electors of each municipal corporation, wherein the population exceeds two thousand, shall have power and authority to frame, adopt and amend the charter of such corporation

claim: Charters and ordinances are void if they conflict with general law
quote: shall be invalid and void if inconsistent or in conflict with this constitution or the general laws of the state

claim: A city charter must provide how candidates file and are nominated and how primaries and regular elections run
quote: shall provide a method and time for the filing of certificates of candidacy, nominating candidates, conducting primary and regular municipal elections

claim: General election law applies to municipal elections except as a charter provides
quote: Except as otherwise provided in the charter of any municipality, the provisions of general law

claim: Unless the charter says otherwise, a municipality elects a mayor, recorder and council
quote: Unless otherwise provided in the charter of a municipality, there shall be elected a mayor, a recorder and council members, who together shall form the governing body of the municipality.

claim: Without wards there are at least five council members
quote: When a municipality has not been divided into wards or election districts, there shall be at least five council members

claim: Towns and villages may move to four-year terms by vote
quote: Officers of a town or village may be elected for a four-year term upon approval by a majority of the legal votes cast at a regular municipal election of a proposition calling for four-year terms.

claim: The Municipal Home Rule Program is permanent
quote: The Municipal Home Rule Pilot Program is established as a permanent program and shall be identified as the Municipal Home Rule Program.

claim: State election offense and administration articles apply to every municipal election, even under home rule charters
quote: Notwithstanding other provisions of this code or of any special legislative or home rule city charter

claim: Magistrate divisions certify the candidate with the most votes
quote: the board of canvassers shall declare and certify the election of the eligible candidate receiving the highest numbers of votes cast within a numbered division

claim: Circuit judge races with no candidate over 30 percent go to a November runoff
quote: there shall be a runoff election at the subsequent general election between the two candidates who received the highest and next-highest number of votes cast in that division

claim: School board elections certify the top vote-getters for full terms
quote: Declare and certify the election of the required number of eligible candidates receiving the highest numbers of votes to fill any full terms

claim: Section 3-1-31 lists 2025 SB 50 in its bill history
quote: 2025 Regular Session SB50
